title: Progressive Hypertrophy PPL
author: Torrey Saxton
desc:
Progressive Hypertrophy PPL is a six-day-per-week Push/Pull/Legs program built for intermediate lifters whose primary goal is muscle growth.

Rather than repeating the same three workouts every week, this program uses a 12-workout rotation over two weeks. Each workout emphasizes a different aspect of development—chest, shoulders, triceps, lats, upper back, biceps, quads, posterior chain, or unilateral stability—while maintaining balanced weekly training volume.

The program is built around a simple double-progression model:

Stay within the prescribed rep range.
Increase repetitions until every prescribed set reaches the top of the range.
Increase the load and repeat.

Compound movements are prioritized early in each workout while isolation exercises provide additional targeted volume. Every major muscle group is trained multiple times throughout the rotation from different movement patterns and resistance profiles.

This program is intended for lifters who:

Want to prioritize hypertrophy over maximal strength.
Prefer training six days per week.
Enjoy more exercise variety than a traditional PPL while maintaining consistent progression.
Want a program that can be run for months without feeling repetitive.

Progression beats perfection. Focus on consistent technique, train close to failure with good form, recover well, and let progressive overload drive long-term muscle growth.
